In the Australian parliamentary system, the Parliament also serves as the highest legislative body. This mapping represents the highest legislative bodies in the two political systems.

Prime Minister corresponds to Prime Minister: In the British parliamentary system, the Prime Minister is the highest leader of the government. In the Australian parliamentary system, the Prime Minister is also the highest leader of the government. This mapping represents the government heads in the two political systems.

House of Commons corresponds to House of Representatives: In the British parliamentary system, the House of Commons is a component of Congress, representing the people from various electoral districts in the UK. In the Australian parliamentary system, the House of Representatives is also a component of Parliament, representing the people from various electoral districts in Australia. This mapping represents the people's representative bodies in the two political systems.

House of Lords corresponds to Senate: In the British parliamentary system, the House of Lords is another component of Congress responsible for deliberating and passing laws. In the Australian parliamentary system, the Senate is also another component of Parliament responsible for deliberating and passing laws. This mapping represents the legislative bodies in the two political systems.

background.source: The British Parliamentary System, also known as the Westminster system, is a type of parliamentary government that originated in England. It utilizes a range of procedures for operating a legislature, with key aspects such as an executive branch made up of members of the legislature who are accountable to it, parliamentary opposition parties to ensure a balance of power, and a ceremonial head of state who is separate from the head of government. The system is named after the Palace of Westminster, which houses the Parliament of the United Kingdom, and it is used in the national and subnational legislatures of most former colonies of the British Empire. This includes countries such as Canada, Australia, and New Zealand, as well as former British Hong Kong. While some colonies have since adopted different systems of government, the Westminster model remains an important foundation for many democratic governments around the world. Within the British Parliamentary System, the Parliament is comprised of two houses - the House of Commons and the House of Lords - and they work alongside the Prime Minister and Congress to make critical decisions.
background.target: The Australian parliamentary system is a form of democratic governance in which the executive branch derives its legitimacy from the support of the legislature, known as the parliament. This system is characterized by having a separate head of state, and the head of government is accountable to the parliament. The parliament is composed of two chambers: the House of Representatives and the Senate. The Prime Minister is the head of government, and is typically a member of the House of Representatives. The Australian parliamentary system is based on the Westminster system of parliamentarianism, which was developed in the UK. With its bicameral parliament and Prime Minister as head of government, the Australian parliamentary system is a classic example of this form of government.
